subject: Re: Procurement & compliance — commercial path (PO vs card) & marketplace interest
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>

Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Subject: Quick recap & next steps from today's call — procurement path and security gating

Hi Amelia — great to meet virtually today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of call:
- Harbor Bank is evaluating Redwood for a supervised POC (customer support summarization use case).
- Primary procurement preference for enterprise purchases: PO (Net 30). Team is open to card for initial POC if Redwood can provision a short-term trial.
- Security/compliance gating: your security team needs SOC 2 Type II evidence, a completed security questionnaire, and confirmation on DPA terms before finance will enable a PO. Marketplace (AWS/GCP) listing would be a strong accelerant for procurement but is not a strict requirement.

Attachments I’ve included: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (current DPA we typically sign), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (high-level report + auditor contact), SOW-POC-draft.xlsx (template for POC & pricing scenarios).

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you introduce your procurement contact (name + email)? We asked that so we can route the PO templating and payment terms questions directly.
2) If security prefers, we can schedule a 30–45m call between your security team and our security engineer (Dev Patel) to walk through SOC 2, data residency, and the questionnaire.
3) Confirm whether you’d prefer we start the POC on card (faster) or wait for a PO (predictable billing).
4) If marketplace listing matters, we can provide an initial checklist; full listing typically takes 4–6 weeks depending on AMS/GCP paperwork.

If that looks right, I’ll (a) loop in Dev for the security call and (b) reach out to your procurement once you share the contact.

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few quick answers: 

- Procurement contact: Tom Nguyen (tom.nguyen@harborbank.com) — I’ve cc'd procurement in this reply. Tom runs vendor onboarding for Platform & Data.
- Payment preference: For anything above $50k ARR they request a PO; we can do a card to spin up a short POC but procurement needs to own the commercial agreement for production.
- Security: Security will need the full SOC 2 Type II report (not just a summary) and the completed security questionnaire. They'll likely ask for encryption-at-rest specifics and any data processing subprocessors.
- Marketplace: Harbor Bank prefers marketplace purchases if available (AWS Marketplace). If Redwood is not listed by the time we finalize, procurement can still proceed via PO, but listing would speed approvals.

Can you send the full SOC 2 report and a link to where we can download or complete your standard security questionnaire? Also please confirm whether Redwood will accept our redline of the DPA or prefer a standard counter-signed copy.

I'll coordinate Tom's availability for a short kickoff call once we have the SOC 2 and questionnaire.

Best,
Amelia Brooks
Director, Customer Success
Harbor Bank

Thanks Amelia — looping Tom in. Tom / procurement team — great to e-meet. Short plan from our side to close the compliance + procurement items quickly: 

1) Security artifacts: I’ve attached a SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf in the initial email; Dev will share the full SOC 2 report and a completed security questionnaire PDF in a separate secure link by end-of-day today. If you prefer an S3 download link or secure portal access, mention preference.

2) DPA & redlines: Our legal team prefers to start from Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and accepts standard commercial redlines. If you send Tom's redline as markups, Marissa (cc'd) will review and aim to get back within 48 hours for most standard requests. If there are material changes (data residency, subprocessors), we may need legal sync.

3) Payment path: We can provision a card-based trial within 48 hours for a demo/POC. For production purchase on PO, we typically need a signed SOW and PO reference. I attached an SOW-POC-draft.xlsx with two scenarios (card-based trial; PO with 12-month contract).

4) Marketplace: Redwood is actively pursuing AWS Marketplace onboarding. If Harbor Bank can wait 4–6 weeks, the listing would make procurement easier; if not, we can proceed via PO.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Tom: please confirm preferred secure transfer method for SOC 2 and send any procurement templates you want Redwood to complete.
- Tom/Amelia: share any mandatory fields for SOW/PO (billing address, legal entity, tax ID).
- Dev Patel: I’ve asked Dev to be available for a 45-minute security deep-dive; suggested slots tomorrow 10-11am or Thursday 2-3pm PT.

If Tom is available, can we do a short kickoff call tomorrow at 11am PT? If not, propose two alternative times and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOC 2 full report link in a separate secure email.

Best,
Karthik

Karthik / Amelia — thanks for the summary and for looping me in. A few items from procurement: 

- We prefer PO for anything > $50k. Tentative budget for a first-year engagement: $120k (subject to final SOW).
- For the SOC 2 report: please send the full auditor report via a secure link (we can accept a time-limited S3 link or a DocuSign/secure download). We will not start commercial contracting until security confirms.
- For the DPA: we will return a redlined DPA (typically minor changes). Please have your legal team ready for a 48–72 hour review turnaround.
- For speed, we are open to a card-based POC for up to 30 days while we run the security review. If Redwood can provision the trial with a credit card, that will let us validate the technical fit while procurement completes paperwork.

I can make 30 minutes available tomorrow 9:30–10am PT for a kickoff. If that works, we can cover secure transfer preferences and required SOW fields.

Tom Nguyen
